feature_contracts.scope: static interface binding; behavioral results are verified separately

requirements.requirement: Expose firmware-visible CSR/MMIO configuration and status registers with address, write-data, read-data, valid, write-enable, and ready semantics.
Decode compact 128-bit host request records and produce compact 128-bit response records.
Validate opcode, sequence ordering, freshness/age, packet length indicators, and optional integrity metadata.
Maintain a single in-flight command shadow and minimal sequence/watchdog state.
Clamp command values to programmable bounds before forward propagation when validation succeeds.
Assert and latch protocol, stale, timeout, and clamp-related status for software observability.
Prevent unsafe actuator command output after timeout or any validation failure.
Keep all externally visible outputs registered and synchronous.
All outputs are registered and change only on clk edges.
The top shall not instantiate the surrogate model in RTL.
A request is accepted only when req_valid and req_ready are asserted together and the decoded packet satisfies all protocol, freshness, sequence, and integrity checks.
Sequence duplication or out-of-order behavior is rejected when the corresponding CSR policy enables ordering enforcement.
Freshness/age is compared against a programmable stale threshold; stale packets are rejected.
Watchdog starts on request acceptance and is cleared only by valid response acceptance, explicit host heartbeat, or firmware clear action as implemented in CSR control.

If the watchdog expires, timeout fault is asserted, command validity is suppressed, and the timed-out session remains blocked until software clears the fault or a new valid session is established according to CSR policy.
When a command is valid and all safety checks pass, actuator_cmd_value is clamped within configured bounds before being registered and forwarded.
If any validation fails, actuator_cmd_valid must be deasserted and actuator_cmd_fault must be asserted; no silent substitution of a fallback command is permitted.
CSR writes update configuration registers only through registered decode logic.
CSR reads reflect current status registers, sticky fault bits, sequence tracking, watchdog state, and configuration values.
Formal assertions shall capture: no unsafe command after timeout, no command acceptance when stale, clamp within bounds, and safe reset baseline.

On reset, all safety state initializes to benign safe values: command outputs are invalid, faults are cleared, sequence tracking is reset to a deterministic baseline, watchdog state is cleared, and CSR readback returns reset-defined default
Decode 6-bit CSR addresses into implemented registers and fields.
Expose writable configuration fields for enable, sequence policy, stale threshold, watchdog limit, bounds, default mode, and sticky-fault clear.
Expose readable status fields for mode, sequence, watchdog, and fault indicators.
Provide ready/acknowledge semantics for CSR transactions.
Clear sticky faults when commanded by firmware through the CSR interface.
Every implemented register field must be reachable via the decode map.
Writes only affect writable fields; read-only status fields are not directly writable.
Sticky-fault clear is pulsed or level-encoded as implemented, but only through a CSR write to the designated register.
CSR responses must be deterministic and registered.
No registers other than the declared fields are software-visible.

On reset, configuration registers initialize to safe defaults with enable deasserted, sequence enforcement enabled, stale threshold and watchdog limit set to conservative safe values, bounds set to neutral-safe limits, default mode cleared
Decode and validate request opcode, sequence number, freshness/age metadata, length indicators, target, bounds index, and optional integrity metadata.
Manage request acceptance and ready/valid handshake for host transport.
Generate response packets with acknowledgment, fault codes, watchdog status, and command summary.
Maintain watchdog state and timeout detection.
Latch protocol, stale, clamp, and timeout faults according to policy.
Drive actuator command outputs only when request acceptance and safety checks succeed.
Use only minimal control metadata and one in-flight command shadow.
The request-valid/request-ready handshake governs acceptance; no implicit acceptance is allowed.
Out-of-order or duplicate sequence behavior is rejected when sequence enforcement is enabled.
Stale requests are rejected according to the programmable threshold.
Unsupported opcodes, malformed packets, invalid length indicators, and integrity failures are rejected.
Command clamping is applied only after a request is otherwise valid; if any validation fails, cmd_valid remains deasserted.
Timeout forces safe-active status and suppresses command validity until cleared.
Response emission must be compact and deterministically derived from the accepted request and status state.
No fallback command may be substituted on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions.

On reset, transport outputs deassert valid, response data is cleared to a deterministic reset encoding, watchdog and sequence tracking are reset, faults are cleared, the command outputs are invalid, and the payload/history buffer interface
Expose the memory macro interface for RTL generation and downstream collateral.
Preserve the declared memory macro port interface.
Memory macro contents are not reset by the controller reset.

notes: This is a conformance analysis, not a formal proof.
Missing or partial items should be reviewed and turned into executable assertions/tests where needed.
